function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been known since ancient times—Thales of Miletus (c. 600 BCE) observed static electricity from rubbing amber. However, the systematic study and naming of the phenomenon began in the 17th and 18th centuries:

| Scientist | Contribution |
|-----------|--------------|
| **William Gilbert** (1544–1603) | First to use the word *electric* (from Greek *ēlektron*, meaning amber) and distinguished between magnetism and static electricity. |
| **Benjamin Franklin** (1706–1790) | Coined the term *electricity* in his 1751 essay “An Essay on Electricity.” He also conducted famous kite experiments that demonstrated the electrical nature of lightning. |
| **Alessandro Volta** (1745–1827) | Invented the first chemical battery (the voltaic pile), providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **Hans Christian Ørsted** (1777–1851) | Discovered the relationship between electricity and magnetism (electromagnetism). |
| **Michael Faraday** (1791–1867) | Developed the principles of electromagnetic induction, laying the groundwork for electric generators and motors. |

So while no single person “discovered” electricity, it was the collective work of many scientists—especially William Gilbert and Benjamin Franklin—that turned the phenomenon into a recognized field of study.
